newsitem.title: ROMANIA: RADIO ROMANIA AFTERNOON HEADLINES AT 4 PM.
newsitem.headline: RADIO ROMANIA AFTERNOON HEADLINES AT 4 PM.

text.p: * Romanian government started its weekly meeting with a presentation on the preparations for Sunday's parliamentary and presidential polls.
The cabinet is expected to debate the draft of the state budget for 1997.
* Prime Minister Nicolae Vacaroiu denied reports by the Romanian Oil Company saying petrol prices would rise by up to 16 percent at the beginning of 1997.
* All presiding judges at all polling stations across the country must run checks of their stations on Saturday, prior to voting.

* The whole staff of each polling station -- judges and party representatives -- must be present at 5 a.m. at the polling stations on Sunday for the voting to effectively start at 6. a.m. as forseen by the law.

* Some 6 million ballots for the presidential polls will be reprinted for seven of Romania's 42 counties and the capital Bucharest to include the electoral signs of three independent candidates, a Central Electoral Bureau (BEC) official said.
Printing is expected to be completed by Friday night.

* There are 133 foreign observers accredited for the November 3 polls, most of them representing the Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe (OSCE) and the Council of Europe's parliamentary assembly, BEC officials said.
They said 43 foreign journalists were accredited, too.
* Parliament speaker Oliviu Gherman met OSCE observers to discuss procedures related to Sunday's vote. Observers asked for votes cast on so-called "special lists" to be counted and checked.

* Winter energy reserves have been completed with fuel oil and coal stocks up 10 percent from last year, industry ministry senior official Gavrila Georgescu told a news conference. -- Bucharest Newsroom 40-1 3120264
